LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Message.RequireReload: Changed settings will take effect after loading a save or restarting the game.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Note.DefaultOff: Disabled by default (you can still enable it manually):
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Note.FastListerRemove.Skip: [Skipped] {0} has already rewritten the same code, so this optimization is not active in this session and the other implementation is used instead.
[Skipped] The removal call could not be located in the vanilla method, most likely because another mod rewrote it. This optimization is not active in this session.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DebugOutput.Desc: Output debug info to the console. Enabling this may slightly reduce game speed, as the game records the entire stack trace for each console message, which is an expensive operation.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.VectoredExceptionHa: Access violations, illegal instructions, stack overflows and failed page reads kill the game instantly, and managed code never sees any of them - the CLR does not surface these to UnhandledException. This option installs a native Windows exception handler that writes the fault site (RIP + module offset, access kind and address) to YaOpt_Crash_<pid>.log in the Logs folder of the save data folder before the process dies, plus stack frame candidates for a stack overflow. Each fault code is recorded at most 4 times, then only counted, so gameplay is not slowed. It cannot prevent the crash; CLR fail-fast (0xC0000409) cannot be intercepted from user mode, so a full managed stack still requires a crash dump (DOTNET_DbgEnableMiniDump=1, DOTNET_DbgMiniDumpType=4). Windows only. Requires a game restart to take effect.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.EnhancedCrashLog.De: Writes the managed UnhandledException stack with method names and source lines into YaOpt_Crash_<pid>.log in the Logs folder, alongside the native VEH fault record. On the next launch, the newest previous crash report is copied in full to YaOpt_Crash-prev.log and a preview is printed in the game log; every other report is deleted, so the Logs folder keeps only this session's report and that copy. Requires a game restart to take effect.
Redirects the process stderr to YaOpt_Crash_<pid>.log without buffering, so text the runtime prints on its way out (for example the repeating function names of a stack overflow) is appended to the same report. Automatically disabled when [WG] WOWGAG's Performance Patch is loaded, or when stderr is already a file or console, so this mod never takes over a global handle another mod uses. Windows only. Requires a game restart to take effect.
Caps how many toils a pawn can advance through in a single tick. Vanilla runs the next toil's start action on the current stack frame, and some toils finish instantly (an instant toil, or a move to a cell the pawn already occupies). A toil graph that keeps jumping back into such a toil therefore recurses until the stack overflows, which kills the game instantly and cannot be caught. Excess advances are postponed to the next tick; a pawn that still cannot advance for one second has its job ended with an error instead of freezing forever. Normal jobs never reach the limit, so there is no gameplay impact. Requires a game restart to take effect.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MaterialGetColor.De: Caches material colors to reduce the overhead of frequent calls to the underlying engine function. The cache is automatically updated when the material color changes.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GlowGridCombine.Des: Replaces the light color combine pass with a section-indexed implementation. Vanilla tests every light for every dirty cell, so placing a light-blocking wall near a lamp can trigger millions of rect tests per frame. The replacement only visits the lights that overlap the cell's section, while keeping the accumulation order identical so light colors do not change.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GasGridTick.Desc: Skips empty 64-cell buckets in the gas dissipation and diffusion sweeps using a one-bit-per-cell occupancy bitmap, instead of probing a fixed number of cells every tick regardless of where the gas is. Each cell is still processed at the same rate, so the gas simulation result is unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FleckTickLoop.Desc: Updates each fleck's game-tick state in place instead of copying the struct out of the list and writing it back. Fleck motion, lifetimes and removal are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FleckFastDraw.Desc: Uses the identity rotation instead of building a quaternion for flecks that are drawn with zero rotation. The rendered result is identical.
Builds each new fleck directly inside its system's list instead of constructing it separately and copying it in. Fleck data and ordering are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FleckAutoInstancing: Scans every fleck def and enables GPU instancing where its shader declares the instance transform and color buffers that batching needs. Flecks rendered through per-fleck property blocks are left alone. Rendering result is unchanged; loading a save or restarting is required for the change to apply.
Flecks whose shaders do not declare the instance buffers keep the vanilla per-fleck path. Off by default.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.SoundOneShotManager: Replaces the per-sound LINQ counts and the per-frame cleanup scan in the one-shot sound manager with direct scans and in-place removal. Which sounds play, their voice priority and their order are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ColoredText.Desc: Optimizes the parsing performance of rich text (e.g., colored text). The vanilla game uses a slow overload of IndexOf (involving culture-sensitive checks) to locate tags. This optimization replaces it with a faster overload that performs a direct ordinal comparison.
Starts the render preparation for dynamic objects earlier. While vanilla supports parallel preparation, it starts after the static terrain is drawn. This optimization dispatches the preparation jobs before drawing the terrain, allowing worker threads to process object data concurrently with the main thread's terrain rendering, effectively hiding the latency.
Mods that draw during the render preparation step get their graphics covered by terrain.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PrepareBatchCount.D: The vanilla game uses a large batch size for parallel render preparation. However, rendering costs vary greatly between objects (e.g., pawns vs. items), and objects are often clustered (e.g., raids). This leads to thread imbalance where some threads finish early while others struggle with heavy batches. This optimization reduces the batch size, allowing the work-stealing algorithm to distribute the load more evenly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelMaterialUpd: Moves material parameter updates to the parallel rendering preparation phase. Vanilla performs these on the main thread, even though they usually don't require it. If a mod overrides material updates for specific objects (which might be unsafe), this optimization will automatically fall back to the main thread for those objects.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastRecacheRequeste: Optimizes the check for whether an object needs to regenerate render parameters. Vanilla checks this by recursively calling every child node in the render tree. Since 97% of render trees are shallow (less than or equal to 4 layers), this optimization inlines the check for the first 4 layers into a single function, avoiding virtual function call overhead. Note: Performance profiler shows only a minor improvement. This optimization may be removed in future versions.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Des: Vanilla loads all mod textures into VRAM at startup. This optimization loads textures only when they are first requested, reducing startup time and VRAM usage, but causing stutters when textures are loaded in-game. Note that texture unloading is not yet implemented, so VRAM usage may eventually reach peak levels during long play sessions.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Com: Skews the stats of Graphics Settings+ and ImageOpt.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Dds: Only enable lazy loading for DDS textures (and Zstd compressed DDS from ImageOpt). Non-DDS formats require extra time to convert to a renderable format upon loading, causing noticeable stuttering during runtime loading.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LazyTextureLoad.Rad: Basic optimization only delays the loading of textures for pawns and items. Due to vanilla code, building textures are always loaded at game startup to generate texture atlases and serve as preview icons. Enabling this option will downsample textures larger than 256 pixels to 256 pixels at game startup, loading the full texture only when actually used in the game. Because loading detection is required when creating things, it slightly increases the overhead of thing creation, resulting in a slight increase in stuttering during game loading and when a large number of objects are created on the map. It is recommended to enable this option only if VRAM usage is still tight after enabling basic optimization. Furthermore, this option only supports DDS (and Zstd compressed DDS) textures.
Optimizes XML patch operations by simplifying common XPath expressions. If an XPath expression matches a simple pattern like "Defs/DefType[defName='DefName']", this optimization bypasses the complex XPath engine and uses a faster direct node lookup. This speeds up the game startup process.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastTranslationInje: Optimizes the process of injecting translation text into XML data at startup. The game checks for errors such as duplicate field injections. The vanilla implementation performs this check with O(N^2) complexity. This optimization replaces the linear search with a hash table lookup, reducing the complexity to O(N). This speeds up game startup, especially for non-English languages.

Duplicates [WG] WOWGAG's Performance Patch's "Reuse type-name lookup result" (Loading tab): this one removes the duplicate-check loop, that one only skips the scan, so only this one takes effect when both are on. Nothing to turn off, and no need to disable that option for this.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RuntimeInfoCache.De: Caches type information at startup to accelerate Harmony type retrieval. This speeds up Harmony patch processing for some mods, improving game startup time in modded environments. It has no effect in a vanilla environment.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FixTextureAtlas.Des: Fixes a vanilla bug where texture atlases smaller than 512x512 have Mipmaps enabled but not populated, causing visual corruption (colored stripes) when zooming out. This issue typically affects scatterable items (e.g. pebbles) from high-res texture mods. It occurs in specific mod combinations where the atlas size falls into the problematic range.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MapMeshUpdateThrott: Throttles the update frequency of the map mesh (terrain rendering). In vanilla, any change in snow or dust thickness triggers an immediate mesh update in the rendering frame, consuming significant resources during frequent changes (e.g., snowfall or melting). This optimization imposes a minimum real-time interval between updates. The map is forcibly updated when the game is paused.

Adjusts the minimum real-time interval between two updates. Note that since the game uses incremental updates for terrain, this option has diminishing returns. Setting the interval to 1000ms won't reduce update overhead to 1/10th of 100ms, because the number of cells to process per update increases. Recommended values are 300 or 500. If you don't care about visual lag, 1000 is also acceptable.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PRNRWorker: Pawn Render Node Worker Cache Fix
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PRNRWorker.Desc: The initialization of PawnRenderNodeProperties.Worker is slow. The game has a built-in cache for it. However, due to a coding oversight, the cache will never be read. This optimization fixes the bug to correctly use the cache.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PRNRWorker.Compatib: Not compatible with mods that change PawnRenderNodeProperties.workerClass at runtime.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GraphicTextureCache: Caches the textures required for Graphic_Multi initialization. Vanilla constructs texture paths for all four cardinal directions using string concatenation and performs asset lookups every time. This optimization caches the resolved textures, eliminating these redundant operations. Originally designed for Humanoid Alien Races, but benefits any mod that frequently rebuilds graphics. Note: This optimization may cause texture hot reload in developer options to fail.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapTextureCach: Caches repeated texture-path resolution for every ContentFinder<Texture2D>.Get call; world-map layers that query once per tile benefit most. Vanilla scans every loaded mod on each lookup and falls back to Resources.Load when needed; this turns repeated queries into dictionary hits and clears the cache when mod content reloads.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapSubMeshCach: World draw layers linearly scan their submesh list for a material once per world tile. This caches material-to-index mappings per layer and invalidates them when a submesh fills or submeshes are reset or disposed, preserving vanilla split ordering.
Duplicates the equivalent feature in WOWGAG's Performance Patch.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapInsectLayer: VFE Insectoids' insect layer scans every settlement for each world tile. This flattens insect territories into a set so tiles outside them are skipped directly, reducing world-map rebuild time with large mod lists.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapRegrowth.De: ReGrowth's beautification layer rebuilds texture paths and resolves materials for every world tile, although the result only depends on biome, hilliness, and temperature/rainfall bands. This resolves those combinations once per biome, preserves drawing and random-call order, and caches repeated mod-setting reads.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapRegrowth.St: Experimental. This replaces ReGrowth's beautification rebuild method; disable it manually if world-map textures look wrong. Incompatible versions, missing required members, or conflicting patches disable it automatically.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldMapLandformsPa: On the first world-map rebuild after loading a save, fills Geological Landforms' world-tile cache with up to 16 workers before drawing in vanilla order. Each tile is computed independently into its own cache slot; generation logic and drawing results are unchanged.
Only applies to versions of Geological Landforms without the WarmCache parallel fill.
Uses up to 16 workers; automatically disabled on conflicts and with Multiplayer.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.Silhouette.Desc: Optimizes the lookup performance of the silhouette (off-screen icon) cache by implementing a better comparison mechanism.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ToggleTabCheck.Desc: A hideable tab (e.g. the Mechanoid tab) is asked whether it should be disabled over and over: one UI pass asks four to five times (drawing, the visible-count and the hotkey check), and a frame can run several passes. Some modded tabs have no cache at all and scan the map on every ask. This optimization lets the later asks of the same frame reuse the first answer; every new frame recomputes, so nothing on screen lags by more than one frame.
Render preparation rebuilds each node's matrix with up to five separately built 4x4 multiplications and a full inversion of a translation matrix. Vanilla still marks the method [BurstCompile], but 1.7's Burst runtime is a no-op stub, so it runs as ordinary managed code. This replaces it with a fused implementation that collapses the whole chain into one affine multiply, removes the inversion, and runs the rotation path on SIMD lanes.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingGetComp.Desc: Vanilla GetComp is fast when finding an existing component but very slow when looking for a missing one. Unfortunately, the only way to check if a component exists is to query it and wait for a failure. This optimization rewrites the lookup mechanism to ensure fast failure when searching for non-existent components.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.De: Introduces limited multithreading for pawn updates. Multithreading handles pawn job interruption checks and constant job checks.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.St: If the error log shows "ParallelPawnTickManager" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Co: Mods must not produce side effects or run non-thread-safe code when checking job failure conditions - the check can run twice in one frame (once in the parallel predictor, once on the main thread).
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Mu: Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Jo: Predicts whether a pawn's current job will fail (e.g., target unavailable) in the current frame. If it's predicted not to fail, the check on the main thread is skipped; otherwise, the main thread re-runs the standard check to ensure correctness.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPawnTick.Co: Predict whether a constant job will be executed in the current frame. A constant job refers to a high-priority action, such as evading enemies or searching for oxygen in space.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelWorkGiver.D: Work issuance is one of the most performance-intensive operations in the game. It normally iterates through a prioritized list of allowed works until a valid one is found. This optimization uses multi-threading to check this list. When a thread finds a valid work, it truncates the search sequence at that point (discarding lower-priority works), waits for other threads checking higher-priority works to complete, and then issues the highest-priority valid work found.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelWorkGiver.S: If the error log shows "ParallelWorkGiver" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelWorkGiver.C: Mods must not produce side effects or run non-thread-safe code when deciding whether to issue work, and must not assume issued work always runs: several candidates can be produced at once and only the highest-priority one is taken.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelWorkGiver.M: Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelPostMapTick: Executes map steady environment effects, water freezing and gas diffusion updates using multi-threading.
If the error log shows "SteadyEnvironmentEffects", "TempTerrainManager", or "GasGrid" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ParallelThoughtUpda: Executes pawn thought updates using multi-threading.
If the error log shows "ParallelThoughtCreatingJob" or "ParallelThoughtUpdater" in the call stack, try disabling this optimization.
Uses multi-threading and is automatically disabled when the Multiplayer mod is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdeoCheck.Desc: Optimizes the check for whether an Ideoligion allows a specific action. Vanilla iterates through all precepts to make this determination. This optimization creates a cache of precepts that impose restrictions whenever precepts are updated. When checking permissions, it only iterates through these cached restrictive precepts, ignoring irrelevant ones.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.BedThrottle.Desc: Optimizes the bed availability check for lying pawns. The vanilla game checks the availability of the current bed for lying pawns every tick, which is necessary but involves some heavy calculations, such as determining whether a sick pawn has recovered. After throttling, a full check will be performed every 15 ticks (0.25 seconds), and the other 14 ticks will only perform simple, quick, and necessary checks, such as determining whether the bed is destroyed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.BedThrottle.Compati: Duplicates Performance Fish (FailOnBedNoLongerUsable) and [WG] WOWGAG's Performance Patch's "Bed usability check interval" (Tick rate tab); only one takes effect. Performance Fish checks every 64 frames only, which is faster; this one checks more often, which is safer. Bed unavailability is rare, so Performance Fish is the better trade.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdleThrottle.Desc: Throttles the interruption idle check for idle pawns (sleeping and wandering) in the game. This optimization includes two configurable parts:\n1. Optimizes the check interval for lying pawns waking up to work. In the vanilla game, lying pawns would perform a work check every 211 ticks. This optimization can extend this interval and also make the interval dynamic, controlling it based on the number of lying colonists, ensuring that pawns in small colonies can still respond quickly to emergencies.\n2. Optimizes the work check interval for idle pawns. In the vanilla game, idle colonists would perform a work check every 125~200 ticks. This optimization can extend this interval and also make it dynamic, controlling the interval based on the number of colonists with nothing to do.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdleThrottle.Compat: Duplicates [WG] WOWGAG's Performance Patch's "Lying-down urgent job check interval" (Tick rate tab); only one takes effect. This one derives the interval from the number of lying colonists, that one uses a fixed interval (422 ticks by default, adjustable 211-1266).
Adjusts the check interval for lying pawns to get up and work, in ticks. The vanilla value is 211 ticks.
Controls the check interval for lying pawns to get up and work based on the number of lying colonists.
Check interval when the number of colonists lying in bed is less than or equal to the minimum number, in ticks. The vanilla value is 211 ticks.

The check interval when the number of colonists lying in bed is greater than or equal to the maximum number, in ticks. When the number of lying colonists is between the minimum and maximum number, the interval is calculated using linear interpolation.
The check interval will be minimized when the number of colonists in bed is less than or equal to this number.

When the number of colonists in bed is greater than or equal to this number, the check interval will reach its maximum. When the number is between the minimum and maximum number, the check interval will increase linearly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.IdleThrottle.StopWa: Adjusts the check interval for idle pawns to find work, in ticks. The vanilla value is at least 125 ticks.\nThe actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.\nThe random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1}
Controls the check interval for idle colonists looking for work based on the number of idle colonists.

Adjusts the check interval when the number of idle colonists is less than or equal to the minimum number, in ticks. The vanilla value is at least 125 ticks.\nThe actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.\nThe random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1}

Adjusts the check interval when the number of idle colonists is greater than or equal to the maximum number, in ticks. When the number of idle colonists is between the minimum and maximum number, the interval is calculated using linear interpolation.\nThe actual check interval will have a random fluctuation to distribute the work check over the game time to avoid stuttering.\nThe random fluctuation range will be {0} ~ {1}
The check interval will be minimized when the number of idle colonists is less than or equal to this number.

When the number of idle colonists is greater than or equal to this number, the check interval will reach its maximum. When the number is between the minimum and maximum number, the check interval will increase linearly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WindUpdate.Desc: Vanilla updates wind strength parameters for all plant materials every logic tick, which is unnecessary. This optimization restricts these updates to render frames only.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastListerRemove.De: Optimizes the efficiency of removing objects from the game. Vanilla searches through lists linearly to remove objects. This optimization tracks object positions using indices, allowing for direct removal by swapping the removed object with the last one in the list.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastListerRemove.Co: Duplicates [WG] WOWGAG's Performance Patch and GUIPerformancePatch's "Faster thing list removal" (Tick rate tab). This one's index lookup is faster than the other's end-of-list scan, so turn theirs off and restart to use this.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FastSpawnedThingsRe: Indexes the map's spawned-things container so despawn removal uses an O(1) dictionary lookup and swap-remove instead of a linear search plus list shift. The index is built lazily and falls back to vanilla behavior if it ever becomes stale.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GenTypesLockFree.De: Reads Type.IsSealed directly instead of locking and querying the vanilla cache. ThingWithComps.GetComp uses this after a missing component-type lookup to skip scanning when T is sealed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.InfoLogNoStack.Desc: Skips stack-trace capture and formatting for Info-level log messages. Vanilla captures a full stack with file info for every log line, which costs several microseconds and several KB per message. Info entries therefore no longer include a stack trace in Player.log or the in-game log window; Warning, Error and their console stack frames are unchanged. Changes require a game restart.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnLabelCache.Desc: Caches pawn name labels and their measured widths for a short period. Vanilla rebuilds the label string and measures it at least twice per rendered pawn per frame; cached values refresh every 60 frames, so renames appear with at most a small delay.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.TurretTargetPrune.D: Player-faction turrets skip the full target search when the map has no hostile, aggro or factionless candidates for the player faction. Manned turrets and other factions are left to vanilla. The early-out only removes a search over an empty candidate set, so it does not add work when targets exist.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.TurretTargetPrune.C: Mods that replace turret targeting may conflict.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.TempTerrainPrune.De: Skips the water-freezing pass on cells whose terrain cannot freeze. Vanilla reads the cell temperature and room before checking canFreeze; for most land cells this check avoids that work, and freezable cells still run vanilla unchanged. This option is shown only while Temporary Terrain Merge is disabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.TempTerrainMerge.De: Runs the per-cell freeze and melt passes as one pass: the cell temperature is read once, room lookups happen only after the corresponding random roll succeeds, and the radial scans check terrain before resolving rooms. The random stream, the freezing chance and the resulting ice are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.TempTerrainMerge.Co: Mods that patch the freeze/melt passes or their terrain filters may be bypassed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RegionQueryFast.Des: Reads the region grid directly when no region rebuild is pending, instead of running the rebuild check and a second bounds check for every region and room lookup. Dirty grids, a disabled updater, a disposed grid and out-of-bounds cells keep the vanilla path, including its logging. Nothing is cached, so no invalidation is needed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RegionQueryFast.Com: Mods that patch RegionAt or GetValidRegionAt may be bypassed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.CameraUpdateRate.De: The game calculates the visibility of things on the screen every tick and reduces the update rate of off-screen things. However, this calculation is a bit complicated, incurring some overhead. This optimization fine-tunes the visibility check, slightly relaxing the criteria and reducing the overhead of update rate calculation. The trade-off is that under certain conditions, a few things close to the screen edge but invisible may be mistakenly identified as visible, causing the system to increase their update rate and resulting in runtime overhead. However, in most cases, this optimization is worthwhile.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.GetMapPawns.Desc: Optimizes the code for retrieving pawns on the map in the game, eliminating some redundant calculations. In addition, it also reduces the workload of determining childcare. In the vanilla game, when searching for hungry babies, it searches not only for those already on the map but also containers, a step that accounts for a large portion of the computation. Therefore, this optimization only performs a full map container search every three checks, and the other two checks only examine babies outside of containers.
Optimizes target finding calculations during combat, eliminating some redundant calculations.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ListerBuildingsCach: Indexes colonist buildings by def and answers ColonistsHaveBuilding, AllBuildingsColonistOfDef and ColonistsHaveBuildingWithPowerOn from that map-local index. The index is built on first use and maintained when buildings are added or removed; list results are copied into the vanilla result buffer and empty results stay cached, so callers cannot corrupt the index.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ImmunityCache.Desc: Caches the list of diseases that can currently be immunized against until the pawn's hediff list changes. Vanilla rebuilds that list on every health tick for every pawn.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.InvisibilityCache.D: Answers IsPsychologicallyInvisible, IsHiddenFromPlayer and GetAlpha from a cached per-pawn state instead of scanning the hediff list. Vanilla runs those scans several times per visible pawn per frame.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ShamblerIdleThrottl: Stretches the shambler's idle target search from 900-1800 ticks to 15000-17499 ticks. Shamblers with a target, a delayed alert, or an engagement within the last 180 ticks keep vanilla timing; damage, lord alerts and nearby shamblers still assign targets immediately.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RefuelSearchCache.D: Reuses the best-fuel and all-fuel searches once between refuel validation and job creation, and supplies a per-map refuel candidate list. The list is maintained on spawn and despawn; vanilla validation still checks fuel level, auto-refuel settings, fog, reservations and other dynamic conditions. The list is only used for the global fallback after the normal local scan.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DeathThoughts.Desc: Finds death witnesses within 12 cells instead of scanning every living pawn, deduplicates multi-cell pawns so they cannot stack witness thoughts, and limits relation-specific thoughts to relation candidates. General lost thoughts still cover map, world and temporary pawns; cross-map witness checks are omitted.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DeathThoughts.Compa: Mods that rewrite death or rescue thoughts may be bypassed.
Optimizes the recursive search of thing containers, reducing the overhead of checking non-container contents.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MeditationTick.Desc: Throttles the meditation update frequency from every tick to once every 100 ticks (with 100x effect compensation). Meditation is surprisingly expensive, especially for tribal psycasters scanning for Anima grass every frame. Note: This slightly impacts gameplay, as partial progress (avg. 50 ticks / 0.83s) is lost when meditation is interrupted.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MeditationTick.Comp: Compatible with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded; may conflict with mods that heavily change meditation. Duplicates Performance Esmolas' "Meditation Throttle", which wins if both are installed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.StatCache.Desc: Extends the vanilla stat caching system to include Comfortable Temperature and Filth Rate. Comfortable Temperature is updated every 20 ticks (and forcibly refreshed when apparel changes), while Filth Rate is updated every 60 ticks. This reduces the overhead of frequently accessing these expensive stats.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LearningStatCache.D: Caches GlobalLearningFactor for 120 ticks, so Learn calls stop rerunning the full stat pipeline every time. Gene, hediff, trait, apparel, equipment or ideo changes can take up to 120 ticks (about two seconds) to affect learning speed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ImmunityStatCache.D: Caches ImmunityGainSpeed for 20 ticks. Every immunity record re-evaluates this stat on every health interval, even though it changes rarely. Food, rest, bed, resting or age changes may take up to 20 ticks (about a third of a second) to affect immunity gain.
Caches the Nutrition stat for 20 ticks inside FoodUtility.NutritionForEater, the call every AI food search goes through. Vanilla re-evaluates each candidate food's nutrition for every pawn on every scan. The eater's RawNutritionFactor is still evaluated separately for each eater. Dynamic nutrition changes from mods may take up to 20 ticks to affect food choice.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DrugPolicyCache.Des: Replaces the linear drug-policy entry lookup with an index and reuses the scheduled-drug job priorities for the current tick. With many drug defs the two drug job givers otherwise rescan the whole policy several times per job search. Hits are revalidated against the policy, so edits in the drug policy window take effect immediately.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DrugScheduleCache.D: Reuses the scheduled-drug decision for the current tick. The drug job giver evaluates every policy entry once for its priority and again when it builds the job. The cached decision is dropped when a drug is ingested or a suspension ends, and it is never kept while paused.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PrioritySorterSnaps: Computes each candidate's job priority once per selection pass. Vanilla recomputes every remaining priority after each failed candidate, so an idle pawn performs about a hundred priority checks per job search. The selection order and tie break are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.MoodThoughtDedup.De: Skips a second situational thought rebuild in the same tick when the first rebuild already produced fresh data. Only the redundant same-tick pass is removed; the result is unchanged.
Caches the MoveSpeed stat for 20 ticks at the movement call site. Vanilla re-evaluates MoveSpeed for every cell a pawn walks even though it rarely changes. With this enabled the same value is reused for up to 20 ticks (about a third of a second). Revenants are excluded because their speed follows a visibility-time curve. Recent changes to gear, health, or light may take up to 20 ticks to affect movement speed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PsychicEntropyCache: Caches PsychicEntropyMax for 20 ticks at the MaxEntropy and MaxPotentialEntropy getters. This avoids repeating the full stat calculation in neural heat gizmos and casting paths. Disabled by default because gear, gene or hediff changes can take up to 20 ticks to appear.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.CelestialSunGlowCac: Reuses the current map's celestial sun glow for the rest of the same tick. Sky, lighting, shadow and weather code often ask for the identical value repeatedly. The cache is keyed by map identity and absolute tick, so results do not lag and gravship movement needs no special Tile check.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.FrameWorkToBuildCac: Remembers Frame.WorkToBuild by buildable def and stuff instead of rerunning the abstract stat calculation for every construction tick and progress read. Uses flat Def-index arrays for the common no-stuff case and lazy per-def stuff caches. Disabled by default; caches clear on load and after vanilla stat-base writes.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingSetMakerSample: Reuses an item-set sample when the same merged parameters, seed and game tick repeat. Quest reward and event item generation runs the same deterministic sample once per option to build the weighted table and then again for the chosen one. The sample is seeded, so the produced items and the random stream are unchanged. Samples also read world state such as colonist titles and research progress, so entries expire every tick and are cleared on load.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingSetMakerStatCa: Within one item-set sample, remembers each candidate's minimum, maximum and single-item value instead of asking the stat system up to three times. Only vanilla value callbacks are memoized, and the cache is thrown away when the sample ends.
Caches three def-only lookups used while generating items: whether a melee weapon material is a derp choice, the allowed material list of each def, and the recipe used to price a def without an explicit market value. Values refresh when a save loads; a mod that patches one of these methods disables that part instead of being bypassed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGenerationIndex: Uses single-threaded indexes and caches during pawn generation: required apparel lookup, one-pass filtered apparel weights, one-pass relation sample weights, Rosaline birth-parent lookup, and gene notification batching. Apparel indexing requires the gear rewrite. Each part falls back independently when a patch or a missing method makes it unsafe; no generation work is moved to another thread.
Known Humanoid Alien Races, Rosaline and RPEF relation patches are explicitly recognised.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGenerationFailu: Stops degenerate generation data from aborting pawn generation. When every candidate implant is worth zero, vanilla picks null and then reads its market value; a null entry in techHediffsRequired reaches the install path; and a faction leader whose 120 generation attempts all failed is dereferenced without a check. Each guard only skips that entry or reports "no leader", and the random stream and normal results are unchanged. Enabled by default.
Implemented as transpilers, so other patches on the same methods still run. If the vanilla method shape changes, the guard is skipped and vanilla behaviour is kept.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGearSessionCach: Reuses values that stay constant during one apparel or weapon generation call. Apparel generation retries up to 80 candidate sets and re-runs the same material restrictions and pawn temperature stats on every attempt; weapon selection evaluates every candidate weight twice. The memo lasts only for that one call, so the random stream and the produced gear stay identical to vanilla.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGearRebuild.Des: Replaces the random-retry selection of apparel and weapons with a constructive one. Apparel generation no longer rebuilds and re-validates the whole candidate set up to 80 times: candidates are filtered once, torso and leg coverage are seeded, and the budget is filled with weighted picks that cannot overlap or exceed the budget. Weapon selection evaluates each candidate weight once instead of twice. Mutual exclusivity, budget, required items, race restrictions and naked rules are preserved, but the exact random sequence is no longer identical to vanilla. Disabled by default.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGearRebuild.Com: With Humanoid Alien Races loaded, HAR's pool patches are neutralised and pairs are filtered per race. Passer Race's apparel restriction context runs before the rewrite, and known gear postfixes still execute.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGearEnvironment: Uses the Pawn's destination map environment when available instead of world-tile seasonal averages: current outdoor temperature, the map's current pollution with toxic fallout, and the destination biome's vacuum state. The map is resolved once per Pawn and all checks are constant-time field reads with no new allocations; without a resolvable map the rewrite falls back to the exact vanilla calculations. Only effective while Pawn Gear Generation Rewrite is enabled. Disabled by default.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnGearHarFastPath: Answers Humanoid Alien Races' apparel restriction lookups directly. HAR's apparel-properties lookup allocates a closure on every call even when its cache hits, and its wearable postfix queries race restrictions even when vanilla already returned false; apparel generation calls both once per candidate pair. The replacement map reproduces HAR's first-match def lookup and is rebuilt when defs change.
Only active with Humanoid Alien Races loaded. If HAR's methods are missing or changed, the patches are skipped and HAR keeps its own behaviour.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnApparelPairCach: Reuses the headgear, wearable, apparel tag and seeded generate-chance answers for each apparel definition while the pawn, headgear flag and fixed seed stay the same, which holds for the whole candidate scan. The budget stays outside the cache and prices remain per pair. A different pawn or cached parameter clears the cache, so results match the vanilla checks.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnBackstoryMatchC: Replaces the allocating backstory category check with an allocation-free one and caches the match result per filter as a bitmap. Every shuffled backstory slot evaluates one filter against all loaded backstories, and the result only depends on the filter and the def data. The cache is rebuilt when defs change.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.PawnTraitsHarFastPa: Validates each trait definition against Humanoid Alien Races' race restrictions once per trait generation instead of on every weighted sampler pass and draw. HAR's check builds the pawn's backstory restriction list and rolls its chances each time, so the materialised candidate list removes most of the work. Trait count, conflicts, work tags and black/white lists are still enforced by vanilla.
Only active with Humanoid Alien Races loaded. HAR's chance rolls run once per candidate instead of once per sampler pass, so the exact random sequence is not preserved.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingSetMakerCanGen: Answers the CanGenerate check for item-set options from the first sampling iteration instead of running the whole sample. Option tables ask every option whether it can generate before picking one, so the full sample used to run several times while only one option was generated. The first iteration already decides whether any item can be produced; the material pool and values are still built exactly like vanilla, and the random stream is unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.QuestLodgerFastPath: Checks all extra-faction quest parts once for either a home or mini faction, instead of collecting and deduplicating the full list twice. No results are cached and all vanilla quest, refugee and affected-pawn conditions are preserved. Helps most when several extra-faction quest parts are active.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.QuestSelectionFastP: Builds a weighted random order from the cheap natural root weights, then runs CanRun in that order until the first valid root. Selection probability follows the natural root weight, while roots after the first valid one avoid the expensive CanRun check. Roots accepted by the current planet layer are preferred, with a weighted fallback if none passes. Disable this to restore the exact vanilla chooser.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.QuestAncientComplex: When the weighted scan finds no quest, tries the Ancient Complex quest roots before giving up. Only has an effect while the quest selection fast path is enabled.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.QuestPointsNormaliz: When a quest is generated with points at or below zero, derives points from the incident target's current threat points, or reuses the value computed moments earlier by the fast selector. Explicit positive points and Slate values are preserved. This repairs dev tools and edge callers that would otherwise generate rewards with zero threat value.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Note.Conflict.QuestMethodP: Another mod patches the quest generation method ({0})
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Note.Conflict.QuestMethodM: The 1.7 quest generation method was not found
For pawns without an ideo, checks the DrugDesire trait directly instead of allocating two history events that are always accepted anyway. Pawns with an ideo keep the original path, including random checks, so behaviour and RNG are unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ConstructDeliverRes: Optimizes the check order of resource delivery during construction. The vanilla game checks passability twice when assigning construction jobs; this optimization removes the redundant check. Also adds a cache for internal passability calculations, improving performance when laying lots of floor and walls.
Optimizes performance for map connectivity updates (e.g., building or removing walls). The vanilla code uses a large deduplication pool and repeatedly clears it within a loop, causing significant overhead. This optimization replaces it with a smaller deduplication pool and moves the clearing operation outside the loop, improving performance.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.HARNeedCondition.De: Humanoid Alien Races allocates a two-element HashSet<Type> every time a pawn's need level is written, adding up to tens of KB of garbage per frame. HAR only reads that argument, so this optimization passes one shared static set instead. Behavior is unchanged.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.LocalDateCache.Desc: Caches the current day tick, hour, day percent and season of each map for the rest of the tick. Every one of these lookups rebuilds the map tile centre from the planet mesh to get a longitude, and the sky, weather and celestial code ask for the same map's date a dozen times per tick. Results are identical to vanilla; only the repeated work is skipped.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RecipeUsersCache.De: Caches the list of things that can run a recipe instead of rescanning every thing def each time. Vanilla rebuilds this by walking the entire def database on every call. The cache is discarded when the def list or the recipe's own user list changes, and invalidated periodically in case a mod edits a thing def's recipe list directly.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DefLookupCache.Desc: Builds one index of the def-wide recipe and research lookups after defs load. A thing's recipe list, a recipe's user list, a research project's unlocks and the research prerequisite map are answered from the index instead of rescanning every def each time, including from other mods' startup constructors. The index is rebuilt on every load and dropped when defs are torn down.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.DefLookupCache.Comp: Known recipe and research result patches are composed into the index.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.BiomeAnimalIndex.De: Builds each biome's wild animal list and commonality table in one pass after defs load. Vanilla scans every animal kind on each access, and its lazy commonality table throws on duplicate entries and stays incomplete. The index merges duplicates instead, keeping the higher commonality.
Persists the draw offsets GiddyUp computes at startup. GiddyUp renders and pixel-scans every life stage graphic on each launch; this option seeds its session cache from a checked file and drops only the entries whose graphic changed.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ExosuitXmlFast.Desc: Replaces Exosuit's full-document class-rename patch operation with a value-only walk over a prepared lookup table, so the XML patching pass no longer rebuilds the class-name table for every node.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.ThingDefBaseStatCac: Remembers the base mass, base flammability and base hit points of every thing def after the game starts. Vanilla recalculates each one through the full stat system every time. Mostly helps mods that read these values in bulk; vanilla itself rarely asks. Values only refresh when a save is loaded.
Remembers the Beauty and BeautyOutdoors values of every terrain def after the game starts. BeautyUtility asks for the terrain value once per sampled cell, and abstract stat requests have no Thing for the vanilla stat caches to key on. Values only refresh when a save is loaded.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.WorldPawnsListCache: Reuses the world pawn lists instead of rebuilding them on every access. Vanilla clears and refills them from the alive, mothballed and dead sets each time, even when nothing changed. The lists are rebuilt as soon as a pawn is added or removed, so callers see the same contents as vanilla.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.StorableDefsCache.D: Remembers which thing defs can be stored, instead of rescanning every def each time a storage filter is reset. That scan checks several properties on several thousand defs, which adds up when a storage settings window resets filters repeatedly. Invalidated periodically to pick up defs a mod edited after load.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RoomThingsCache.Des: Remembers the list of things in a room instead of rebuilding it, and de-duplicating it through a hash set, on every read. One room stat update reads that list a dozen times while scoring the room. Rebuilt as soon as anything in the room is added, removed or moved.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RoomStatsThrottle.D: Limits a room to one stats and role recompute every 128 ticks. Vanilla recomputes as soon as the room is read after any item inside it spawns or despawns, and each recompute runs every room stat and room role worker, so a busy stockpile can trigger it several times per second. Reads in between return the previous values.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.RoomStatsThrottle.C: Room stats, the room role label and mood thoughts based on the room can lag by up to about two seconds.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.AlertThrottle.Desc: Measures how long each alert's recalculation takes and schedules it by cost. Cheap alerts keep the vanilla cadence; expensive ones are checked less often, at most once every 5 seconds (High priority once every 2 seconds). Critical alerts are never delayed. The first few seconds after a game loads are used to learn the costs.
LanguageData.YaOpt.Setting.Option.AlertThrottle.Compa: Alerts can appear or disappear up to one scheduling interval late. Mods that already replace AlertsReadoutUpdate (performance analyzers or other alert throttlers) may prevent this patch from applying; a YaOpt warning is written to the log when that happens.
